Previously initialization only constructed the connection with stored credentials. A transient Salesforce OAuth outage (or rate limiting) now blocks all Salesforce calendar operations that previously worked with valid stored tokens — a real regres

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the diff shows that lines 72-88 add an unconditional fetch call to 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token' during the initialization of the Salesforce connection (in the constructor or connection setup). This happens before the jsforce.Connection is created. Unlike other integrations that use refreshOAuthTokens which conditionally refreshes based on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the Salesforce implementation makes this token refresh call unconditionally every time. This means if the OAuth endpoint is temporarily unavailable, the entire Salesforce adapter initialization will fail, even if the existing stored access_token is still valid and could be used.
